latest_release.body:
## Release highlights

- **Russian and Turkish**: Purge now runs in Russian and Turkish. Storage sizes on the Overview and in the sidebar also follow your language's units and your region's decimal separator.
- **More leftovers found**: The App Uninstaller now finds an app's scripts, cookies and website data, its hidden files, and its caches, preferences and logs in the shared Library folder.
- **Xcode's Metal Toolchain**: Dev Tools lists Xcode's optional Metal Toolchain, about 900 MB, and removes it with Xcode's own tool. It is Check First and is deleted permanently.
- **uv cache**: Dev Tools now offers uv's package cache, which can grow to tens of GB. It is Check First.
- **Apple Intelligence errors in full**: When removing the Apple Intelligence models fails, a Details button shows everything macOS answered, ready to copy into a report.

## What's changed

* feat: remove Xcode's optional Metal Toolchain with xcodebuild (#132) by @jithin-sabu in #340
* feat: add Russian (ru) localization (#342) by @alexkirov288-hub in #341
* fix: show and log the full error when an Apple Intelligence removal fails (#343) by @jithin-sabu in #344
* fix: localize the storage unit and decimal separator by @alexkirov288-hub in #347
* fix: add the Russian text for the Apple Intelligence error details and storage units (#343) by @jithin-sabu in #348
* feat: offer the uv cache as Check First (#345) by @jithin-sabu in #349
* feat: add Turkish localization by @dermanonline in #350
* feat: find app leftovers in more Library folders (#352) by @jithin-sabu in #356
* test: pin that the Quick Look thumbnail cache is never offered (#353) by @jithin-sabu in #357
* docs: bring the README in line with the app (#358) by @jithin-sabu in #359
* fix: correct the Russian custom interval, admin prompt and delete sheet text by @jithin-sabu in #360
* docs: close the gaps left in the Chinese and Russian READMEs by @jithin-sabu in #361

## Thanks

* @alexkirov288-hub for the Russian translation in #341 and the localized storage units in #347
* @dermanonline for the Turkish translation in #350
* @RayBB for asking for the uv cache in #345
* @BertonYang1229 for reporting the Apple Intelligence removal failure in #343

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jithin-sabu/purge-app/compare/v1.14.1...v1.15.0

See the assets below to download and install this version.

detail.readme:
Purge

Free up your Mac. Safely.

English | 简体中文 | Русский | Українська

A free, open-source native Mac app that clears the cache and junk your Mac piles up on its own.
Files go to the Trash by default, so you can put them back.

Download  ·  Install guide  ·  Build from source  ·  Security

--- Your Mac quietly fills up with cache and junk you never see and never asked for. Purge finds it, marks what is safe, and clears it in one click. > [!NOTE] > Files and folders go to the Trash by default, and Purge never empties the Trash, so you can put them back until you empty it yourself. Deleted permanently: iOS simulators and simulator runtimes, through Xcode's `simctl`; Xcode's optional Metal Toolchain, through `xcodebuild -deleteComponent` (Xcode downloads it again when a project needs it); Time Machine local snapshots, through `tmutil` (Purge keeps the newest and the one from your last backup); the Apple Intelligence models on macOS 27, which Apple's asset service releases and Purge can download again; command-line tools and Homebrew cask apps that their package manager uninstalls, when you choose that in the review sheet. Docker Desktop's folder goes to the Trash. Purge does not run `docker system prune`. You do not need to understand any of it to use it. But if you ever want to check, every item carries a plain-language explanation and a safety label, so nothing gets touched that you cannot see and verify first. --- ## Features ### Overview - **Where your space went**: one bar for the whole disk. Used, free and total come straight from the volume, so they match System Settings. App Caches, Dev Tools, Large Files, installed apps and leftovers from deleted apps each get their own segment, and the rest is shown as everything else - A row per category with its size and share of the disk. Click one to open its tab - **Everything else** opens too. Click the row and a page shows what it holds: four figures for what you can do about the space, over a map where each group is a frame with its biggest folders drawn inside, sized by space and coloured by kind. The kinds are space you free in another app (Photos, Mail, Steam, the Trash), your own files (projects, documents), what Purge leaves alone because it doesn't consider it safe to delete (caches off its list, app data no installed app claims), and what macOS manages. Point at a tile to name it, and click it to see what it is, with Show in Finder or the owning app's own way to free it. It is read only: nothing on it moves a file - **Scan Everything** (⇧⌘R) scans every category, one at a time so the Mac stays responsive. When you open Purge it does the same on its own. Large Files, the app list and leftovers need Full Disk Access. Without it Purge still scans App Caches and Dev Tools, and skips the places macOS protects, such as sandboxed apps' caches - Each byte is counted once: an app's cache folder counts under App Caches, not again under the app - **Hidden in System Data**: a card under the categories for space macOS counts as System Data. Its **Time Machine snapshots** row is where you remove local snapshots, and on macOS 27 it also holds the Apple Intelligence models - **Apple Intelligence models** (macOS 27, Apple silicon): the on-device models macOS files under System Data, with no switch to remove them. Remove releases them through Apple's asset service and installs a profile, which you approve once, so they don't download again. Download Again asks you to remove the profile in System Settings, then asks macOS for the sets Purge removed, in your Siri language. The size shown is Apple's figure; Purge records what the disk really gave back ### App Caches Scans `~/Library/Caches`, sandbox container caches (these need Full Disk Access), and common system junk: - Per-app cache folders with friendly names, brand icons, and a plain-language explanation if you want to read it - System Junk like application logs, crash reports, macOS installers, and leftover macOS update files - Large media caches from creative apps like Premiere Pro and After Effects - Duplicate cache locations for the same app merged into a single row - Results stream in as they are found ### Dev Tools Five groups in one view: - **Global dev tool caches**: Xcode (Derived Data, Archives, DeviceSupport), Homebrew, npm, pnpm, Yarn, CocoaPods, Gradle, the Dart and Flutter pub cache, Docker Desktop, VS Code, Cursor, JetBrains, Cargo, Terraform, and more - **iOS Simulators**: every simulator that is shut down, one row each. A running simulator is listed so its space is counted, but it can't be selected - **Simulator Runtimes**: one row per runtime that `simctl` reports as deletable - **Xcode Components**: Xcode's optional Metal Toolchain (about 900 MB), removed with `xcodebuild -deleteComponent` when a full Xcode lists it as installed - **Developer projects**: `node_modules`, Python virtual environments, Rust `target`, Flutter build output, Xcode `Pods`, Android `.gradle`, and other artifacts grouped by project Simulators, runtimes and Xcode components are always Check First. They are deleted permanently, not moved to the Trash, and their section headers say so. In **Settings → Cleaning**, choose **Projects count as stale after** (1 month to 2 years, or Show all) to control which projects appear. Age is measured from the last time anything in the project changed, including git activity, not from the date on `node_modules` or `target`. A project in use right now, with a terminal or dev server running inside it or a git command in progress, never appears. Git worktrees made by AI coding tools (Cursor, Codex, Conductor, T3 Code, and Claude Code) appear under **Orphaned Git Worktrees** only once their repository no longer lists them. A worktree Git still uses never appears however old it is, and neither does one a terminal or agent is working inside. ### Large Files Find space-hogging personal files without digging through folders: - Scans **Documents**, **Desktop**, **Downloads**, **Movies**, **Music**, and **Pictures**, plus `~/Parallels` and `~/Virtual Machines.localized` for virtual machines only, and iCloud Drive's own folder for files you can keep only in iCloud - A folder you moved and replaced with a link, such as `~/Documents` pointing to another drive, is scanned where the link leads when that is inside your home folder or on a drive under `/Volumes`, on a disk attached to your Mac. Its files are listed by their real path and go to that drive's Trash. A link anywhere else, such as into `~/Library/CloudStorage`, to a network share, or to a whole drive or a copy of a Mac, is not followed, and the scan says where it leads. Links inside the folders are never followed - Skips managed libraries (Photos, iMovie, Music, and similar), hidden folders, and project folders like `node_modules`, `Pods`, `DerivedData` and build output. Deleting a single file out of a dependency tree only breaks the install, so those belong in Dev Tools, which removes them a folder at a time - **Search** filters the list as you type, matching the file name, the folder it sits in, and its source label - Filter by **size** (5 MB to 1 GB) and **last used** (any time up to over 1 year ago) - Category chips for videos, audio, images, PDFs, archives, documents, AI models, virtual machines, and other files - **Duplicates**: a byte-for-byte scan finds identical copies, groups them together, and shows how much you'd reclaim by keeping one. A **Duplicates** chip gathers them in one place. **Delete extra copies** clears a whole tab of duplicates in one go. It suggests a copy to keep per set and marks the rest for Trash, and you can move the keeper to a different copy before anything is deleted. Nothing is removed until you review and confirm - Sort by size, date, or name; select files and review before deleting - **Quick Look** preview and **Show in Finder** from each row - Deletions move files to **Trash**, so nothing is permanently erased - **Keep Only in iCloud** frees the space an iCloud file takes on this Mac and keeps the file in iCloud, the same as Finder's Remove Download. The **iCloud** chip lists the synced files that also use space here, with how much you'd free, and the action sits there and in each synced file's right-click menu. The file stays in its folder in Finder with a cloud mark, and opening it downloads it again. Purge offers it only for files fully uploaded to iCloud, with no sync conflict, not set to Keep Downloaded, not hard-linked and unchanged for five minutes. It checks all of that again just before it acts on each file, and skips any file that is open in an app. Files in iCloud Drive's own folder are never offered for the Trash, since trashing them removes them from your other devices. It is never part of Clean Safe Items or a scheduled clean Large Files is separate from cache cleanup: these are your personal files, not rebuildable caches. #### Restore images, virtual machines, and unfinished downloads Some big files carry a label that says what they are. Hover it for the full explanation. - **Restore image**: a macOS `.ipsw`, often 15 to 25 GB. It's only needed to set up a Mac, a device, or a virtual machine. - **Virtual machine**: a Parallels (`.pvm`), UTM (`.utm`), or VMware Fusion (`.vmwarevm`) bundle. It's one row and goes to the Trash whole, never a disk file from inside it. If the app is still installed, the label says to remove the VM there, since the app keeps its own list. A VM whose app is open, or that holds a lock file, stays off the list until you quit the app. - **Unfinished download**: `.crdownload`, `.part`, and Parallels' `.prlupd-part` files, and Safari's `.download` bundle when it sits directly in Downloads. #### Local AI models Downloaded models are often the largest files on a Mac and are easy to forget. They appear in Large Files under the **AI Models** category, one row per model, named the way you installed it, with the app or library that downloaded it as the location. Purge knows the stores of **Ollama**, **LM Studio**, the **Hugging Face Hub** cache (`~/.cache/huggingface/hub`; `HF_HOME` and `HF_HUB_CACHE` are honoured when they are set for apps, not only in a shell profile), swift-transformers, apps that keep models under `~/Library/Caches/huggingface`, **PyTorch Hub**, **Whisper**, **GPT4All**, **Jan**, **DiffusionBee** and **Draw Things**. Weight files over 100 MB in `~/Library/Caches`, `~/Library/Application Support` and `~/.cache` that belong to no known store are listed too, by the folder they sit in, so you can tell which app downloaded them. Purge understands Ollama's content-addressed storage, so a model's size counts only the bytes that would actually be reclaimed rather than blobs shared with another model. A Hugging Face model is its whole cache folder, so a blob two snapshots share is counted once and never removed from under the other. Models always go to the Trash and are never part of Clean Safe Items or a scheduled clean. When an app keeps its own list of installed models that Purge can't update, the row says the app may still show the model as installed. ### App Uninstaller Dragging an app to the Trash leaves most of it behind: caches, preferences, containers, saved state, logs, cookies and website data, and login helpers pile up on disk. The Uninstaller removes the app and those leftovers in one pass. - Lists the apps you installed in **Applications** and **~/Applications**, in the **Applications** folder at the top of any drive you plug in, and in folders you add under Settings > Where Purge looks for apps (or from the hint under the app list), skipping system apps and Purge itself. Each tile shows what an uninstall would free: the app bundle plus the leftovers Purge matched to it - Apps from one vendor that share a folder, such as the four apps in `/Applications/DaVinci Resolve`, show as one entry that opens to its apps - Select one or more apps, then review a sheet with a section per app that lists every item with its path and size - Matching is strict, so uninstalling one app can't sweep in files shared across a vendor's apps. Every match arrives checked, and you untick what you want to keep. Three kinds start unticked: a hidden folder in your home folder that holds the app's settings, an Application Scripts folder with scripts in it, and anything another installed app still uses, which is held back and marked "Kept, still used by" that app - A running app is asked to quit first, and only gracefully. If it won't, it's left installed and the rest of the batch still goes through - Everything confirmed moves to **Trash** through the same delete engine as the rest of Purge, so it can all come back. The one exception is an app Homebrew installed as a cask: the review sheet offers two buttons, Remove with Homebrew and Move All to Trash, and says that Homebrew deletes the app permanently and runs the cask's own uninstall steps, which can stop its background services and delete its helper tools and installer files permanently too. A cask that installs several apps is never offered to Homebrew. Its leftovers still go to the Trash, and if Homebrew refuses, the app goes to the Trash instead - Optional, off by default: turn on **Review leftovers when an app is deleted** in Settings. A small background watcher then notices when an app leaves one of those folders — even if Purge is quit — opens Purge with just that app's leftovers, and gets out of the way after you confirm or dismiss. Nothing moves without that review. In this review only exact bundle-id and app-group matches inside your home folder arrive checked; looser name-only matches arrive unchecked for you to confirm - Some apps are installed under an administrator, so your account can't move them to the Trash, and the same goes for their leftovers in `/Library`. Turn on **Remove admin-locked apps without a password** in Settings and a small helper that runs as root moves them to your Trash. It moves only paths the uninstaller approved, and leftover macOS update files. On a standard account the setting reads **Remove admin-locked apps**, and Purge asks for an administrator's name and password each time - You can start from Finder too: turn on **Uninstall from Finder's right-click menu** in Settings, then right-click an app and choose **Uninstall with Purge**. Dropping an app on Purge's Dock icon does the same The Uninstaller has two more lists beside **Installed Apps**. Each appears when its scan finds something: - **Leftovers**: files left behind by apps that are already gone, grouped by how Purge matched them to the app. Nothing is selected for you - **Command-Line Tools**: tools installed by a script go to the Trash: the tool's folder in your home folder, the commands in `~/.local/bin` that start it, and its background jobs. Tools installed by Homebrew, npm, pipx, uv or Cargo are removed by that manager's own uninstall, permanently. The confirmation lists the two groups separately ### Safety labels Purge assigns a safety label to every item it recognizes: | Label | Meaning | |-------|---------| | ✅ **Safe to Clean** | Known cache or rebuildable artifact, safe to remove | | ⚠️ **Check First** | May be safe, but could cause inconvenience | Filter with **All**, **Safe to Clean**, or **Check First** (⌥⌘1–⌥⌘3). Sort by size, date modified, or name. Unidentified folders are left out of the list entirely. Purge only shows what it knows about. The labels and explanations are there to be checked, not read cover to cover. Select the safe items and clean them, or open the reasoning behind any single row first. Either way is fine. ### Cleaning - **Clean Selected**: pick specific rows, review in a confirmation sheet, then delete. Git and lockfile checks run before anything is removed - **Clean Safe Items**: on the Overview, moves every Safe to Clean item to the Trash after one confirmation - **Clean Safe Files**: the same safe cleanup from the menu bar - **Scheduled cleaning**: in **Settings → Cleaning**, turn on **Clean automatically** and choose how often (weekly, monthly, every 3 months, or a **Custom** interval you set in days, weeks, or months). Purge sends a local reminder when a clean is due and runs it the next time you open or switch to Purge, so the cleanup keeps happening without you thinking about it. It never cleans in the background - Files and folders move to the **Trash**. Purge never empties the Trash. iOS simulators and simulator runtimes are deleted permanently through Xcode's `simctl`. The Metal Toolchain is deleted permanently through `xcodebuild -deleteComponent`, and Xcode downloads it again when a project needs it. Time Machine local snapshots are deleted permanently through `tmutil`; Purge keeps the newest and the one from your last backup. The Apple Intelligence models are released through Apple's asset service and can be downloaded again. Tools and cask apps a package manager installed are removed by that manager's own uninstall, permanently, when you pick that in the review sheet ### Settings Settings is a tab in the sidebar (⌘,) with five groups: - **General**: **Keep Purge in the menu bar**, which is off on a new install. When it is on, Purge keeps running after you close the window, and you can also choose **Launch Purge at login** and **Hide Dock icon**. **Appearance** is Auto, Light, or Dark - **Cleaning**: **Clean automatically**, with a frequency and the next-clean date. **Projects count as stale after**, the threshold for Developer Projects. **Excluded folders**, the folders you've told Purge to leave alone, each with its current size. Right-click a row in App Caches, Dev Tools or Large Files and choose **Exclude from scans** to add one. An excluded simulator runtime is listed by name and build, with the size it had when you excluded it. Excluding only ever narrows what Purge looks at - **Uninstalling**: **Uninstall from Finder's right-click menu**, **Where Purge looks for apps**, **Review leftovers when an app is deleted**, and **Remove admin-locked apps without a password** - **Updates and History**: **Check for updates automatically**, **Install updates automatically**, and **Cleaning history**, which lists every automatic and manual clean with the space freed and the item count, and shows a summary of the last one. Open a clean to see what was moved to the Trash, what was deleted permanently, and what was skipped - **Uninstall**: **Uninstall Purge**, covered under [Uninstalling](#uninstalling) ### More - **First-run onboarding**: a welcome, a first scan, and the results with a button that moves the safe items to the Trash. Last comes an optional request for Full Disk Access, shown only if Purge doesn't have it - **Menu bar companion**: recoverable space at a glance, quick open, and scan/clean actions. It is optional and off on a new install; turn on **Keep Purge in the menu bar** in Settings - **Shortcuts and Spotlight**: three actions, Scan for Junk, Clean Safe Junk, and Uninstall an App - **Languages**: the app is in English, Simplified Chinese, Russian and Turkish, and follows your system language - **Disk summary**: the Overview shows used and free space; the sidebar shows what is already in the Trash, and each scan tab's size - **In-app updates**: the About screen checks for, downloads, and installs new versions ### Keyboard shortcuts | Shortcut | Action | |----------|--------| | ⌘R | Scan the current tab (Scan Everything on the Overview) | | ⇧⌘R | Scan Everything, from any tab | | ⌘1–⌘5 | Go to Overview, App Caches, Dev Tools, Large Files, or App Uninstaller | | ⌥⌘1–⌥⌘3 | Filter by All, Safe to Clean, or Check First, on App Caches and Dev Tools | | ⌘F | Search on Large Files and App Uninstaller | | ⌘, | Open Settings | --- ## Download
--- ## Installation There are two ways to install Purge: with Homebrew if you live in the terminal, or by downloading the app directly. Both land in the same place. ### Install with Homebrew ```bash brew install --cask purge ``` This installs Purge from the official Homebrew cask, and Homebrew verifies the download's checksum for you automatically. ### Install manually The steps below walk through the direct download. #### Step 1: Download Click the download link above and download the `.dmg`. #### Step 2: Verify your download (optional but recommended) > [!TIP] > Since Purge deletes files, verifying the checksum confirms your download is byte-for-byte the one that was published, with nothing altered in transit. Each release includes a matching `.dmg.sha256` checksum file. Download both the `.dmg` and its `.dmg.sha256` file into the same folder, then in Terminal: ```bash cd ~/Downloads shasum -a 256 -c Purgev*.dmg.sha256 ``` A result ending in `OK` means the file matches the published release. #### Step 3: Install Open the `.dmg` and drag Purge to your Applications folder. #### Step 4: Open Purge Double-click Purge to open it. Purge is notarized by Apple, so it opens normally with no extra steps. #### Step 5: Let Purge look deeper (optional) Purge works without Full Disk Access: it scans App Caches and Dev Tools. With it, Purge also finds App Store apps' caches, large files, installed apps and deleted apps' leftovers. 1. At the end of the first run, or later from **Look deeper**, click **Let Purge in**. System Settings opens 2. Find Purge in the list and turn on its switch 3. Come back to Purge. It notices the change by itself. If macOS offers to reopen Purge, go ahead Choose **Not now** to skip it. You can turn the access off anytime in System Settings. --- ## Updating Purge updates itself in place. Once a day it checks for a new version, and when one is available the update window appears with the release notes. Choose **Install Update** and Purge downloads it, verifies its signature, installs it, and relaunches. You don't need to visit the release page or drag anything. By default nothing is installed without your confirmation. You can also check whenever you like from the **About** screen, and if you'd rather Purge didn't check on its own, turn off **Check for updates automatically** in **Settings → Updates and History**. If you'd rather not be asked, turn on **Install updates automatically** in the same place, or tick the matching box in the update window. New versions then download in the background and install the next time Purge quits. Once one is ready, **Restart to Update** in the Purge menu, the menu bar menu or the **About** screen installs it straight away. That helps if you keep Purge in the menu bar and rarely quit it. Updates are delivered through [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org), the standard update framework for Mac apps outside the App Store. Each update is signed with a key that lives only on the developer's machine, and Purge refuses any download that doesn't carry a matching signature. ### Updating with Homebrew If you installed through Homebrew, you can update from the terminal instead: ```bash brew upgrade --cask purge ``` Either route is fine. Your settings, cleaning schedule, and history are kept whichever way you update; they live separately from the app. You won't need to grant Full Disk Access again either, since the permission stays with Purge. You can also browse past versions on the [releases page](https://github.com/jithin-sabu/purge-app/releases) anytime. --- ## Uninstalling Choose **Uninstall Purge…** in the Purge menu, or **Settings → Uninstall → Uninstall…**. Purge lists what it runs in the background on your Mac (the deleted-app watcher, the admin helper, the Finder right-click item, the cleanup reminder and launch at login), turns each one off and checks it really stopped, then moves itself to the Trash and quits. Your settings and cleaning history stay on your Mac, so a reinstall picks up where you left off. Tick **Also move settings and history to the Trash** to move them too. Nothing is deleted permanently; you empty the Trash when you're ready. macOS doesn't let an app remove its own Full Disk Access. If Purge had it, the last screen offers **Quit and Open Full Disk Access**. In System Settings, select Purge and click the minus button. Already dragged Purge to the Trash? Download it again, open it, and choose **Uninstall Purge…**, so nothing it ran keeps running. To check nothing is left, Purge should be gone from **System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions**, and this should print nothing: ```bash pgrep -fl io.getpurge ``` --- ## Build from source Prefer to build Purge yourself instead of downloading the release? Here is how. ### Prerequisites - macOS 13.0 or later - **Xcode 26 or later** (from the Mac App Store). The project uses Swift 6.2 build settings (default actor isolation and approachable concurrency) and `@concurrent`, which need Xcode 26; earlier versions won't build it - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 18+ and npm, only needed if you want to regenerate brand icons Dependencies are resolved by Swift Package Manager when you first build. The only one is [Sparkle](https://github.com/sparkle-project/Sparkle), which handles in-app updates. ### Step 1: Clone the repo ```bash git clone https://github.com/jithin-sabu/purge-app.git cd purge-app ``` ### Step 2: Build and run Open the project in Xcode and run: ```bash open purge.xcodeproj ``` Then select the **purge** scheme and press **⌘R**. The project is set to sign with the developer's Developer ID certificate, which you won't have. In Xcode, open **Signing & Capabilities** for each target and choose your own team or **Sign to Run Locally**. Or build straight from the command line, with signing turned off: ```bash # Build a Debug app xcodebuild -project purge.xcodeproj -scheme purge -configuration Debug build CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO # Build a Release app xcodebuild -project purge.xcodeproj -scheme purge -configuration Release build CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ``` The built `Purge.app` is written under Xcode's DerivedData folder (the build output ends with its path). macOS treats each build without your signature as a new app, so Full Disk Access has to be granted again after a rebuild. ### Optional: regenerate brand icons The app cache icons are generated from [simple-icons](https://simpleicons.org). To rebuild them: ```bash npm install npm run generate:icons ``` ### Running the tests ```bash xcodebuild test -project purge.xcodeproj -scheme purge -destination 'platform=macOS' CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ``` The signing flags matter: without a development certificate on the machine, the test build fails before a single test runs. Continuous integration builds the same way. --- ## Requirements - macOS 13.0 or later - Full Disk Access (optional; Large Files, the App Uninstaller and leftovers need it) - Xcode (optional, for iOS simulators and simulator runtimes). If you deleted Xcode, Purge still finds the simulators it left behind --- ## Privacy Purge runs entirely on your Mac. Your excluded folders, cleaning history and last scan stay in its Application Support folder, and your settings in its preferences. Nothing is uploaded. The last scan is saved so Purge has something to show while it scans again. Nothing from Desktop, Documents, Downloads or iCloud is written to it, and Large Files keeps only its totals, by kind of file, never a file name. The one time Purge talks to the network is the update check: once a day it fetches a small XML file from GitHub to see whether a newer version is available. It sends nothing about you or your Mac, and you can turn it off in **Settings → Updates and History**. Purge reads some file contents, on your Mac only. To find duplicates it compares files of the same size byte for byte. To work out which app or tool a file belongs to, it reads small files such as an app's `Info.plist`, LaunchAgent plists, and the scripts that start command-line tools. It never sends file contents anywhere. Purge does not use AI. Nothing you scan or clean is sent to an AI service. --- ## Security Purge deletes files, so safety is the point. A few things worth knowing: - **Trash by default**: Files and folders move to the macOS Trash, and Purge never empties it. You can restore them until you empty the Trash yourself. iOS simulators and simulator runtimes are deleted permanently through `simctl`. Xcode's Metal Toolchain is deleted permanently through `xcodebuild -deleteComponent` and downloads again when a project needs it. Time Machine local snapshots are deleted permanently through `tmutil`; Purge keeps the newest and the one from your last backup. The Apple Intelligence models are released through Apple's asset service and can be downloaded again from Purge. Command-line tools and Homebrew cask apps you choose to remove through their package manager are deleted by that manager, permanently. Docker Desktop's data folder goes to the Trash. Purge does not run `docker system prune`. - **Allowlist-based deletion**: Only paths that match an explicit safety allowlist are ever eligible for cleanup. Anything Purge does not recognize is never touched. The [safety page](https://purgemac.com/safety) lists every allowed location and everything Purge will never touch, generated from the app's source. - **You choose what goes**: Purge shows what is reclaimable and you decide what to clear. - **Root helper, off by default**: To move apps an administrator installed, Purge can install a small helper that runs as root. It stays off until you turn on **Remove admin-locked apps without a password** and approve it in System Settings. It does one thing: it moves a path the uninstaller approved, or a leftover macOS update file, to your Trash. Its source is in `PurgeHelper/`. - **Open source**: The full deletion logic, including the allowlist, is in this repo for you to read or build from source yourself. - **Notarized by Apple**: The app is signed and notarized, so macOS can verify it hasn't been tampered with since release. - **Signed updates**: In-app updates are verified against a signing key before they are installed. An update that isn't signed by that key is refused, so a compromised download can't become a compromised install. Found a safety gap or a path that could be deleted when it shouldn't be? Please report it. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how. --- ## Contributing Bug reports, safety findings, and pull requests are welcome. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) covers how to set up the project and what makes a change easy to review. Anything touching the safety allowlist, the never-delete protections, or the scanning logic gets extra scrutiny and takes longer to review, which is deliberate. Security issues are the exception: report those privately through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) rather than opening an issue. --- ## License Purge is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). You are free to use, read, modify, and distribute it. --- ## Support Purge is free. If it saved you some disk space, you can chip in toward the running costs from the **About** screen inside the app, or directly at [Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/jithinsabu).
---

Purge

释放 Mac 空间，安全第一。

一款免费、开源的原生 Mac 应用，清理 Mac 自己悄悄积累的缓存和垃圾文件。
文件默认移到废纸篓，随时可以放回原处。

下载  ·  安装指南  ·  从源码构建  ·  安全

--- > 本应用的简体中文界面基于 [@zihua-zhang](https://github.com/zihua-zhang) 的社区翻译（[Purge-zh](https://github.com/zihua-zhang/Purge-zh)）。如果本文与英文 README 有出入，请以英文 README 为准。 > > Purge 现在支持英文、简体中文、俄文和土耳其文，并跟随 macOS 的系统语言。你也可以在“系统设置 > 通用 > 语言与地区 > 应用程序”中单独为 Purge 设置语言。 你的 Mac 会悄悄积累大量缓存和垃圾文件，你既看不到，也从没要求过它们存在。Purge 会找出这些文件，标出哪些是安全的，并一键清理。 > [!NOTE] > 文件和文件夹默认会移到废纸篓，Purge 从不清空废纸篓，所以在你自己清空之前都可以放回去。以下内容会被永久移除：iOS 模拟器和模拟器运行时（通过 Xcode 的 `simctl`）；Xcode 可选的 Metal 工具链（通过 `xcodebuild -deleteComponent`，项目需要时 Xcode 会重新下载）；Time Machine 本地快照（通过 `tmutil`，Purge 会保留最新的一张和上次备份留下的那张）；macOS 27 上的 Apple 智能模型（由 Apple 的资源服务释放，之后可以在 Purge 里重新下载）；以及你在检查面板中选择交给包管理器卸载的命令行工具和 Homebrew cask 应用。Docker Desktop 的文件夹会移到废纸篓。Purge 不会执行 `docker system prune`。 你不需要了解其中的细节也能使用。不过，如果你想自己核对，每个项目都附有通俗易懂的说明和安全标签，所以不会有任何你事先看不到、验证不了的内容被动到。 --- ## 功能 ### 概览（Overview） - **空间都去哪了**：用一条横条展示整个磁盘。已用、可用和总容量直接取自磁盘卷，因此与系统设置中显示的一致。应用缓存、开发工具、大文件、已安装的应用以及已删除应用的残留文件，各占一段，其余部分显示为其他内容 - 每个类别一行，显示其大小和占磁盘的比例。点击某一行即可打开对应的标签页 - **其他内容**也可以打开。点击该行会打开一个页面，显示其中有什么：顶部是四个数字，说明你能对这些空间做什么；下方是一张地图，每个分组是一个框，里面按占用空间画出它最大的文件夹，并按类型着色。类型包括：可在其他应用中释放的空间（照片、邮件、Steam、废纸篓）、你自己的文件（项目、文稿）、Purge 认为删除不安全而不去碰的内容（不在清单上的缓存、没有已安装应用认领的应用数据），以及由 macOS 管理的内容。把指针移到某个方块上会显示它的名称，点击可查看它是什么，并提供“在访达中显示”或所属应用自带的释放方式。它是只读的：这里的任何操作都不会移动文件 - **扫描全部**（⇧⌘R）会逐个扫描所有类别，一次只扫一个，让 Mac 保持流畅。打开 Purge 时，它也会自动执行同样的操作。大文件、应用列表和残留文件需要完全磁盘访问权限。没有该权限时，Purge 仍会扫描应用缓存和开发工具，并跳过受 macOS 保护的位置，例如沙盒应用的缓存 - 每个字节只统计一次：应用的缓存文件夹计入应用缓存，不会在该应用名下重复计算 - **藏在“系统数据”中**：位于各类别下方的一张卡片，显示 macOS 计入“系统数据”的空间。其中的 **时间机器快照** 一行用来移除本地快照；在 macOS 27 上，它还包含 Apple 智能模型 - **Apple 智能模型**（macOS 27，Apple 芯片）：macOS 归入“系统数据”的设备端模型，系统没有提供移除它们的开关。**移除** 会通过 Apple 的资源服务释放它们，并安装一个描述文件（你只需批准一次），让它们不会再次下载。**重新下载** 会请你在系统设置中移除该描述文件，然后按你的 Siri 语言向 macOS 请求 Purge 移除的那些模型。显示的大小是 Apple 给出的数字；Purge 记录的是磁盘实际释放的空间 ### 应用缓存（App Caches） 扫描 `~/Library/Caches`、沙盒容器缓存（需要完全磁盘访问权限）以及常见的系统垃圾文件： - 每个应用一个缓存文件夹，带有易懂的名称、品牌图标，以及你想看时可以阅读的通俗说明 - 系统垃圾文件，例如应用日志、崩溃报告、macOS 安装器和残留的 macOS 更新文件 - Premiere Pro 和 After Effects 等创意类应用产生的大型媒体缓存 - 同一应用的重复缓存位置会合并为一行 - 结果会在找到时即时显示 ### 开发工具（Dev Tools） 一个视图中包含五个部分： - **全局开发工具缓存**：Xcode（Derived Data、Archives、DeviceSupport）、Homebrew、npm、pnpm、Yarn、CocoaPods、Gradle、Dart 和 Flutter 的 pub 缓存、Docker Desktop、VS Code、Cursor、JetBrains、Cargo、Terraform 等 - **iOS 模拟器**：每个已关闭的模拟器各占一行。正在运行的模拟器也会列出，以便计入它占用的空间，但无法选中 - **模拟器运行时**：`simctl` 标记为可删除的运行时，每个一行 - **Xcode 组件**：Xcode 可选的 Metal 工具链（约 900 MB），在完整的 Xcode 列出它已安装时，通过 `xcodebuild -deleteComponent` 移除 - **开发项目**：`node_modules`、Python 虚拟环境、Rust 的 `target`、Flutter 构建产物、Xcode 的 `Pods`、Android 的 `.gradle` 以及其他生成文件，按项目分组 模拟器、运行时和 Xcode 组件始终标为“先检查”。它们会被永久删除，不会移到废纸篓，各自的分区标题上也写明了这一点。 在 **设置 → 清理** 中，选择 **项目闲置多久后视为过期**（1 个月到 2 年，或显示全部），来控制显示哪些项目。时间从项目内任何内容最后一次变动算起，包括 git 活动，而不是看 `node_modules` 或 `target` 的日期。正在使用的项目，例如其中正运行着终端或开发服务器，或正在执行 git 命令，永远不会出现。 由 AI 编程工具（Cursor、Codex、Conductor、T3 Code 和 Claude Code）创建的 Git 工作树，只有在其仓库不再列出它们之后，才会出现在 **孤立 Git 工作树（Orphaned Git Worktrees）** 下。Git 仍在使用的工作树无论多旧都不会出现，终端或智能体正在其中工作的工作树同样不会出现。 ### 大文件（Large Files） 不用逐个翻文件夹，就能找到占用空间的个人文件： - 扫描 **文稿**、**桌面**、**下载**、**影片**、**音乐** 和 **图片**，另外只在 `~/Parallels` 和 `~/Virtual Machines.localized` 中查找虚拟机，并在 iCloud 云盘自己的文件夹中查找可以只保留在 iCloud 中的文件 - 你移走并换成链接的文件夹（例如指向另一块磁盘的 `~/Documents`），如果链接指向你的个人文件夹内，或指向 `/Volumes` 下连接到这台 Mac 的磁盘，Purge 会扫描链接指向的位置。其中的文件按真实路径列出，并移到该磁盘的废纸篓。指向其他位置的链接（例如 `~/Library/CloudStorage`、网络共享、整块磁盘或 Mac 的副本）不会被跟随，扫描会说明它指向哪里。文件夹内部的链接一律不会跟随 - 跳过受管理的资源库（照片、iMovie、音乐等）、隐藏文件夹，以及 `node_modules`、`Pods`、`DerivedData` 和构建产物这类项目文件夹。从依赖目录中单独删除一个文件只会破坏安装，所以这些内容应归开发工具处理，它会按文件夹整个移除 - **搜索** 会在你输入时筛选列表，可匹配文件名、所在文件夹及其来源标签 - 按 **大小**（5 MB 到 1 GB）和 **上次使用时间**（不限时间到一年以上）筛选 - 按类别用标签筛选：视频、音频、图片、PDF、压缩文件、文稿、AI 模型、虚拟机和其他文件 - **重复文件**：逐字节扫描找出内容完全相同的副本，将它们归为一组，并显示只保留一份能回收多少空间。**重复文件** 标签会把它们集中在一处。**删除多余副本** 可一次清理整个标签页中的重复文件。它会为每组建议保留一份，并把其余的标记为移到废纸篓，在删除任何内容之前，你可以把要保留的那份换成别的副本。在你检查并确认之前，不会移除任何内容 - 按大小、日期或名称排序；先选择文件，检查后再删除 - 每一行都可使用 **快速查看** 预览和 **在访达中显示** - 删除操作会把文件移到 **废纸篓**，所以不会有任何文件被永久抹除 - **只在 iCloud 中保留** 会释放 iCloud 文件在这台 Mac 上占用的空间，并把文件保留在 iCloud 中，与访达的“移除下载”（Remove Download）相同。**iCloud** 标签会列出同时在本机占用空间的已同步文件，并显示可释放的空间；这个操作就在那里，也在每个已同步文件的右键菜单中。文件仍留在访达中原来的文件夹里，带有云朵标记，打开时会重新下载。Purge 只为满足以下条件的文件提供这个操作：已完整上传到 iCloud、没有同步冲突、未设为“保留下载”（Keep Downloaded）、没有硬链接，并且五分钟内没有改动。在对每个文件执行操作之前，它会再检查一遍这些条件，并跳过正在被应用打开的文件。iCloud 云盘自己的文件夹中的文件永远不会被提供移到废纸篓的选项，因为把它们移到废纸篓会让它们从你的其他设备上消失。它永远不会成为“清理安全项目”或定时清理的一部分 大文件与缓存清理是分开的：这些是你的个人文件，不是可以重新生成的缓存。 #### 恢复映像、虚拟机和未完成的下载 有些大文件会带一个标签，说明它是什么。把指针悬停在标签上可查看完整说明。 - **恢复映像**：macOS 的 `.ipsw` 文件，通常有 15 到 25 GB。只在设置 Mac、设备或虚拟机时需要。 - **虚拟机**：Parallels（`.pvm`）、UTM（`.utm`）或 VMware Fusion（`.vmwarevm`）的虚拟机包。它只占一行，会整个移到废纸篓，绝不会单独移走其中的磁盘文件。如果对应应用仍已安装，标签会提示你在该应用中移除，因为应用自己维护着一份虚拟机列表。如果虚拟机的应用正在运行，或虚拟机中有锁定文件，它会暂不显示，直到你退出该应用。 - **未完成的下载**：`.crdownload`、`.part` 和 Parallels 的 `.prlupd-part` 文件，以及直接位于“下载”文件夹中的 Safari `.download` 包。 #### 本地 AI 模型 下载的模型往往是 Mac 上最大的文件，而且很容易被忘记。它们会出现在大文件的 **AI 模型** 类别下，每个模型一行，名称与你安装时一致，位置显示为下载它的应用或库。Purge 认识 **Ollama**、**LM Studio**、**Hugging Face Hub** 缓存（`~/.cache/huggingface/hub`；`HF_HOME` 和 `HF_HUB_CACHE` 需要对应用生效才会被采用，只写在 shell 配置文件里不行）、swift-transformers、把模型放在 `~/Library/Caches/huggingface` 下的应用、**PyTorch Hub**、**Whisper**、**GPT4All**、**Jan**、**DiffusionBee** 和 **Draw Things** 的模型存储。`~/Library/Caches`、`~/Library/Application Support` 和 `~/.cache` 中不属于任何已知存储、超过 100 MB 的权重文件也会列出，并显示所在文件夹，方便你判断是哪个应用下载的。 Purge 理解 Ollama 的内容寻址存储方式，因此模型的大小只统计真正能回收的字节，不会把与其他模型共享的数据块算进去。一个 Hugging Face 模型就是它的整个缓存文件夹，两个快照共享的数据块只计一次，也不会在另一个快照还需要时被移除。模型始终移到废纸篓，并且永远不会成为"清理安全项目"或定时清理的一部分。如果某个应用维护自己的已安装模型列表而 Purge 无法更新，该行会说明应用可能仍显示该模型为已安装。 ### 应用卸载（App Uninstaller） 把应用拖到废纸篓，大部分内容都会留下：缓存、偏好设置、容器、已保存的状态、日志、Cookie 与网站数据和登录辅助程序都会堆积在磁盘上。应用卸载功能可以一次性移除应用及这些残留文件。 - 列出你安装在 **应用程序** 和 **~/Applications** 中的应用、你接入的任何磁盘顶层 **应用程序** 文件夹中的应用，以及你在“设置 > Purge 在哪里查找应用”中（或通过应用列表下方的提示）添加的文件夹中的应用，跳过系统应用和 Purge 本身。每个图块都会显示卸载后能释放的空间：应用本体加上 Purge 为它匹配到的残留文件 - 同一开发商放在同一个文件夹里的多个应用（例如 `/Applications/DaVinci Resolve` 中的四个应用）会显示为一个条目，展开后可看到其中的各个应用 - 选择一个或多个应用，然后检查一张清单，每个应用一个分区，其中列出每个项目的路径和大小 - 匹配很严格，所以卸载一个应用不会误伤同一开发商多个应用共用的文件。所有匹配到的项目默认都已勾选，你可以取消勾选想保留的内容。有三类默认不勾选：个人文件夹中保存该应用设置的隐藏文件夹、里面有脚本的 Application Scripts 文件夹，以及其他已安装应用仍在使用的内容，这类内容会被保留，并标注“已保留，仍被”该应用“使用” - 正在运行的应用会先被请求退出，而且只会以正常方式请求。如果它不退出，就会保持已安装状态，同一批中的其他应用仍会继续处理 - 所有确认的项目都会通过与 Purge 其他功能相同的删除引擎移到 **废纸篓**，所以都可以恢复。唯一的例外是通过 Homebrew 以 cask 方式安装的应用：检查面板会提供两个按钮，**通过 Homebrew 移除** 和 **全部移到废纸篓**，并说明 Homebrew 会永久删除该应用，还会运行该 cask 自己的卸载步骤，这些步骤可能会停止它的后台服务，并永久删除它的辅助工具和安装文件。会安装多个应用的 cask 永远不会交给 Homebrew 处理。它的残留文件仍会移到废纸篓；如果 Homebrew 拒绝卸载，应用会改为移到废纸篓 - 可选，默认关闭：在设置中开启 **应用删除后检查残留文件**。一个小型后台监测程序会在应用离开上述任一文件夹时发现这一变化（即使 Purge 已退出也一样），打开 Purge 并只显示该应用的残留文件，在你确认或关闭后便不再打扰。没有经过这一步检查，不会移动任何内容。在这项检查中，只有位于个人文件夹内、与 bundle id 和 App Group 完全匹配的项目会默认勾选；只靠名称匹配、较宽松的项目默认不勾选，由你自行确认 - 有些应用是以管理员身份安装的，你的账户无法把它们移到废纸篓，它们在 `/Library` 中的残留文件也一样。在设置中开启 **移除管理员锁定的应用，无需重复输入密码**，一个以 root 身份运行的小型辅助程序就会把它们移到你的废纸篓。它只移动卸载工具已批准的路径，以及残留的 macOS 更新文件。在标准账户上，这项设置显示为 **移除管理员锁定的应用**，Purge 每次都会要求输入管理员的名称和密码 - 你也可以从访达开始：在设置中开启 **在访达右键菜单中卸载**，然后右键点击某个应用并选择 **使用 Purge 卸载**。把应用拖到 Purge 的程序坞图标上，效果相同 除了 **已安装应用**，卸载工具还有两个列表。扫描有结果时，它们才会出现： - **残留文件**：已删除的应用留下的文件，按 Purge 把它们归到该应用的依据分组。不会替你预先勾选任何内容 - **命令行工具**：通过脚本安装的工具会移到废纸篓，包括它在个人文件夹中的文件夹、`~/.local/bin` 中用来启动它的命令，以及它的后台任务。通过 Homebrew、npm、pipx、uv 或 Cargo 安装的工具，由对应管理器自己的卸载命令永久删除。确认面板会把这两组分开列出 ### 安全标签 Purge 会为它识别的每个项目分配一个安全标签： | 标签 | 含义 | |------|------| | ✅ **可安全清理** | 已知的缓存或可重新生成的内容，可以安全移除 | | ⚠️ **先检查** | 可能是安全的，但可能带来不便 | 可用 **全部**、**可安全清理** 或 **先检查** 筛选（⌥⌘1–⌥⌘3）。可按大小、修改日期或名称排序。 无法识别的文件夹会完全不出现在列表中。Purge 只显示它了解的内容。 这些标签和说明是供你核对的，不需要从头读到尾。你可以直接选中安全项目并清理，也可以先展开任意一行查看背后的依据。两种方式都可以。 ### 清理 - **清理所选项目**：选中特定的行，在确认面板中检查，然后删除。在移除任何内容之前，会先进行 Git 和 lockfile 检查 - **清理安全项目**：在概览中，确认一次后把所有“可安全清理”的项目移到废纸篓 - **清理安全文件**：从菜单栏执行同样的安全清理 - **定时清理**：在 **设置 → 清理** 中，开启 **自动清理**，并选择清理频率（每周、每月、每 3 个月，或按天、周、月设定的 **自定义** 间隔）。到期时 Purge 会发送本地提醒，并在你下次打开或切换回 Purge 时执行清理，让清理在你不用惦记的情况下持续进行。它从不在后台清理 - --- ## 安装 安装 Purge 有两种方式：习惯用终端的话用 Homebrew，或者直接下载应用。两种方式的结果相同。 ### 使用 Homebrew 安装 ```bash brew install --cask purge ``` 这条命令会从官方 Homebrew cask 安装 Purge，Homebrew 还会自动为你校验下载文件的校验和。 ### 手动安装 下面的步骤介绍直接下载安装的方式。 #### 第 1 步：下载 点击上方的下载链接，下载 `.dmg`。 #### 第 2 步：验证下载文件（可选，但建议这样做） > [!TIP] > Purge 会删除文件，所以验证校验和可以确认你下载的文件与发布的文件逐字节一致，在传输途中没有被改动。 每个版本都附带一个对应的 `.dmg.sha256` 校验和文件。把 `.dmg` 和它的 `.dmg.sha256` 文件下载到同一个文件夹，然后在“终端”中运行： ```bash cd ~/Downloads shasum -a 256 -c Purgev*.dmg.sha256 ``` 如果结果以 `OK` 结尾，说明文件与发布的版本一致。 #### 第 3 步：安装 打开 `.dmg`，把 Purge 拖到“应用程序”文件夹。 #### 第 4 步：打开 Purge 双击 Purge 即可打开。Purge 已通过 Apple 公证，所以可以正常打开，无需额外步骤。 #### 第 5 步：让 Purge 深入扫描（可选） 没有完全磁盘访问权限，Purge 也能使用：它会扫描应用缓存和开发工具。有了该权限，Purge 还能找到 App Store 应用的缓存、大文件、已安装的应用和已删除应用的残留文件。 1. 在首次启动引导的最后，或之后通过 **深入扫描**，点击 **允许 Purge 访问**。系统设置会打开 2. 在列表中找到 Purge，打开它的开关 3. 回到 Purge。它会自己发现这一变化。如果 macOS 提示重新打开 Purge，照做即可 选择 **暂时不用** 可以跳过。你随时可以在系统设置中关闭这项权限。 --- ## 更新 Purge 会就地自动更新。它每天检查一次新版本，有新版本时会弹出更新窗口并显示发行说明。选择 **安装更新**（Install Update），Purge 会下载更新、验证签名、完成安装并重新打开。你不需要访问发布页面，也不需要拖动任何东西。 默认情况下，没有你的确认，不会安装任何内容。你也可以随时在“关于”界面中检查更新；如果你不希望 Purge 自行检查，可以在 **设置 → 更新与历史记录** 中关闭 **自动检查更新**。 如果你不想每次都被询问，可以在同一处开启 **自动安装更新**，或在更新窗口中勾选对应的选项。之后新版本会在后台下载，并在 Purge 下次退出时安装。更新准备好后，在 Purge 菜单、菜单栏菜单或“关于”界面中选择 **重新启动以更新**，即可立即安装。如果你把 Purge 留在菜单栏、很少退出它，这会很方便。 更新通过 [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org) 提供，这是 App Store 之外的 Mac 应用通用的标准更新框架。每个更新都使用只存放在开发者本人电脑上的密钥签名，Purge 会拒绝任何没有匹配签名的下载。 ### 使用 Homebrew 更新 如果你是通过 Homebrew 安装的，也可以改用终端更新： ```bash brew upgrade --cask purge ``` 两种方式都可以。无论用哪种方式更新，你的设置、清理计划和历史记录都会保留，因为它们与应用本身分开存放。你也不需要再次授予完全磁盘访问权限，因为该权限会一直保留给 Purge。 你也可以随时在[发布页面](https://github.com/jithin-sabu/purge-app/releases)浏览以往的版本。 --- ## 卸载 在 Purge 菜单中选择 **卸载 Purge…**，或前往 **设置 → 卸载 → 卸载…**。Purge 会列出它在你的 Mac 上于后台运行的项目（已删除应用监视器、管理员助手、访达右键菜单项、清理提醒和登录时启动），逐一关闭并确认已真正停止，然后将自身移到废纸篓并退出。 你的设置和清理历史记录会保留在 Mac 上，重新安装后可以继续使用。勾选 **同时将设置和历史记录移到废纸篓** 可一并移走。不会永久删除任何内容；你可以在准备好时自行清倒废纸篓。 macOS 不允许应用移除自身的完全磁盘访问权限。如果 Purge 曾拥有该权限，最后一屏会提供 **退出并打开完全磁盘访问权限** 按钮。在系统设置中选中 Purge，然后点按减号按钮。 已经把 Purge 拖到废纸篓了？请重新下载并打开它，然后选择 **卸载 Purge…**，这样它运行的项目就不会继续运行。要确认没有残留，**系统设置 → 通用 → 登录项与扩展** 中应不再列出 Purge，并且以下命令应没有任何输出： ```bash pgrep -fl io.getpurge ``` --- ## 从源码构建 想自己构建 Purge，而不是下载发布版？方法如下。 ### 前提条件 - macOS 13.0 或更高版本 - **Xcode 26 或更高版本**（来自 Mac App Store）。项目使用了 Swift 6.2 的构建设置（默认 actor 隔离和 approachable concurrency）以及 `@concurrent`，这些都需要 Xcode 26；更早的版本无法构建 - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 18+ 和 npm，仅在你想重新生成品牌图标时需要 依赖项会在你首次构建时由 Swift Package Manager 自动解析。唯一的依赖是 [Sparkle](https://github.com/sparkle-project/Sparkle)，它负责应用内更新。 ### 第 1 步：克隆仓库 ```bash git clone https://github.com/jithin-sabu/purge-app.git cd purge-app ``` ### 第 2 步：构建并运行 在 Xcode 中打开项目并运行： ```bash open purge.xcodeproj ``` 然后选择 **purge** scheme，按下 **⌘R**。 项目设置为使用开发者本人的 Developer ID 证书签名，而你没有这个证书。在 Xcode 中，打开每个 target 的 **Signing & Capabilities**，选择你自己的团队或 **Sign to Run Locally**。 或者直接在命令行中构建，并关闭签名： ```bash # Build a Debug app xcodebuild -project purge.xcodeproj -scheme purge -configuration Debug build CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO # Build a Release app xcodebuild -project purge.xcodeproj -scheme purge -configuration Release build CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ``` 构建出的 `Purge.app` 会写入 Xcode 的 DerivedData 文件夹下（构建输出的末尾会显示它的路径）。macOS 会把每个没有你签名的构建当作新应用，所以每次重新构建后都要再次授予完全磁盘访问权限。 ### 可选：重新生成品牌图标 应用缓存图标由 [simple-icons](https://simpleicons.org) 生成。要重新构建它们： ```bash npm install npm run generate:icons ``` ### 运行测试 ```bash xcodebuild test -project purge.xcodeproj -scheme purge -destination 'platform=macOS' CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ``` 这些签名参数很重要：如果机器上没有开发证书，测试构建会在任何一个测试运行之前就失败。持续集成也是这样构建的。 --- ## 系统要求 - macOS 13.0 或更高版本 - 完全磁盘访问权限（可选；大文件、应用卸载和残留文件需要它） - Xcode（可选，用于 iOS 模拟器和模拟器运行时）。如果你已经删除了 Xcode，Purge 仍能找到它留下的模拟器 --- ## 隐私 Purge 完全在你的 Mac 上运行。排除的文件夹、清理历史记录和上次的扫描结果保存在它的 Application Support 文件夹中，你的设置保存在它的偏好设置中。不会上传任何内容。保存上次的扫描结果，是为了让 Purge 在重新扫描时有内容可以显示。其中不会写入任何来自桌面、文稿、下载或 iCloud 的内容，大文件只保存按文件类型统计的总量，从不保存文件名。 Purge 唯一会联网的时候是检查更新：每天一次，从 GitHub 获取一个很小的 XML 文件，以确认是否有更新的版本。它不会发送任何关于你或你的 Mac 的信息，你也可以在 **设置 → 更新与历史记录** 中关闭它。 Purge 会读取一部分文件内容，但只在你的 Mac 上读取。为了找出重复文件，它会逐字节比较大小相同的文件。为了判断某个文件属于哪个应用或工具，它会读取一些小文件，例如应用的 `Info.plist`、LaunchAgent plist，以及启动命令行工具的脚本。它从不把文件内容发送到任何地方。 Purge 不使用 AI。你扫描或清理的任何内容都不会发送给 AI 服务。 --- ## 安全 Purge 会删除文件，所以安全就是重点。以下几点值得了解： - **默认移到废纸篓**：文件和文件夹会移到 macOS 废纸篓，Purge 从不清空废纸篓。在你自己清空之前都可以恢复。iOS 模拟器和模拟器运行时通过 `simctl` 永久移除。Xcode 的 Metal 工具链通过 `xcodebuild -deleteComponent` 永久移除，项目需要时会重新下载。Time Machine 本地快照通过 `tmutil` 永久移除；Purge 会保留最新的一张和上次备份留下的那张。Apple 智能模型由 Apple 的资源服务释放，之后可以在 Purge 里重新下载。你选择通过包管理器移除的命令行工具和 Homebrew cask 应用会由该管理器永久删除。Docker Desktop 的数据文件夹会移到废纸篓。Purge 不会执行 `docker system prune`。 - **基于允许列表的删除**：只有匹配明确的安全允许列表的路径，才有资格被清理。Purge 不认识的内容，一律不会动。[安全页面](https://purgemac.com/safety)列出了每个允许清理的位置，以及 Purge 永远不会碰的所有内容，由应用的源代码生成。 - **由你决定清理什么**：Purge 会显示哪些空间可以回收，由你决定清理哪些。 - **root 辅助程序，默认关闭**：为了移动管理员安装的应用，Purge 可以安装一个以 root 身份运行的小型辅助程序。在你开启 **移除管理员锁定的应用，无需重复输入密码** 并在系统设置中批准之前，它一直是关闭的。它只做一件事：把卸载工具已批准的路径，或残留的 macOS 更新文件，移到你的废纸篓。它的源码在 `PurgeHelper/` 中。 - **开源**：完整的删除逻辑（包括允许列表）都在这个仓库中，你可以阅读，也可以自己从源码构建。 - **已通过 Apple 公证**：应用经过签名和公证，因此 macOS 可以验证它自发布以来没有被篡改。 - **签名更新**：应用内更新在安装之前会用签名密钥验证。没有用该密钥签名的更新会被拒绝，因此被篡改的下载内容不会变成被篡改的安装。 发现了安全漏洞，或某个本不该被删除的路径可能被删除？请告诉我们。报告方式见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。 --- ##
